package_info.package_manager: CDN (not a package registry, but distributed as a third-party JavaScript asset)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served after February 2024 takeover (exact versioning not applicable; dynamic CDN content)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.js library, previously a trusted open source project, was taken over by a foreign actor who injected malicious JavaScript into the assets served from cdn.polyfill.io. This allowed arbitrary code execution in the browser context of any website including the script, enabling large-scale supply chain attacks such as user redirection, credential theft, and further malware propagation.

execution_context.file_location: Dynamically loaded via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js?..."> in HTML or JavaScript
required_permissions: full JavaScript execution in browser context

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes in the browser context, potentially redirecting users to phishing sites, stealing sensitive information, or propagating further malware by manipulating the DOM or exfiltrating data to attacker-controlled domains.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The CDN, previously trusted, began serving JavaScript with undocumented and unauthorized behaviors, including user redirection and data exfiltration, which are classic signs of a supply chain attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal polyfill libraries only provide compatibility shims for JavaScript features; they should never perform network requests to unknown domains, redirect users, or access sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate polyfill scripts only patch missing JavaScript features and do not interact with the network or user data beyond their intended purpose.
key_indicators: Dynamic JavaScript served from a previously trusted CDN now under new, untrusted ownership
Injected code performing user redirection or data exfiltration
Behavior changes after domain ownership transfer
No version pinning or subresource integrity (SRI) used

execution_context.file_location: Static or dynamic script inclusion in HTML or JavaScript referencing cdn.polyfill.io or related malicious domains
required_permissions: full JavaScript execution in browser context

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the browser fetches and executes JavaScript from cdn.polyfill.io, which may contain malicious payloads that execute in the user's browser context, enabling arbitrary code execution, redirection, or data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Including scripts from a compromised CDN allows attackers to inject arbitrary code into all websites that trust the CDN, enabling mass exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Websites expect third-party CDNs to serve only the intended library code, not arbitrary or malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use is to load polyfills for browser compatibility, but not to execute untrusted or dynamically changing code.
key_indicators: Script inclusion from a domain known to be compromised
Domain ownership and hosting changes to untrusted parties

attack_chain.action: Website includes a <script> tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io, trusting it to provide safe polyfill code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser fetches and executes JavaScript from the CDN.

attack_chain.action: Browser loads and executes the JavaScript payload, which now contains malicious code injected by the new CDN operator.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs in the user's browser context.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs actions such as redirecting users, exfiltrating sensitive data, or further propagating malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: User compromise, data theft, or further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime execution of JavaScript loaded from cdn.polyfill.io or related suspicious domains
Unexpected user redirection or network requests to attacker-controlled domains
Polyfill scripts performing actions beyond feature shimming (e.g., DOM manipulation unrelated to polyfills, credential access, or network exfiltration)
file_indicators: References to polyfill[.]site, polyfill[.]com, bootcdn[.]net, bootcss[.]com, staticfile[.]net, staticfile[.]org, unionadjs[.]com, xhsbpza[.]com, union.macoms[.]la, newcrbpc[.]com in script tags or dynamic script loaders
No use of Subresource Integrity (SRI) for third-party scripts
network_indicators: Outbound requests to cdn.polyfill.io, polyfill.io.bsclink.cn, and other listed suspicious domains
Unexpected network traffic to domains not previously associated with the application
Redirection chains leading to phishing or malware sites
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan all HTML, JavaScript, and template files for script inclusions referencing cdn.polyfill.io or related suspicious domains. Monitor runtime network activity in browsers for requests to these domains. Use static analysis to flag any dynamic script loading from untrusted sources. Implement Subresource Integrity (SRI) and Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict and validate third-party script execution. Alert on any polyfill scripts performing actions beyond feature shimming, such as DOM manipulation, user redirection, or network exfiltration.
